newsitem.title: USA: Wall Street seen firm at open as FOMC meets.
newsitem.headline: Wall Street seen firm at open as FOMC meets.

text.p: Wall Street stocks were expected to open steady to higher Wednesday, with investors nearly certain that Federal Reserve policymakers, wrapping up a two-day meeting, will not raise interest rates.
The Federal Open Market Committee is expected to announce its verdict at around 1415 EDT/1815 GMT.
None of the 36 economists surveyed by Reuters expect the Fed to tighten credit.

"The consensus appears to be steady as she goes for the market," Alan Ackerman, market strategist at Fahnestock & Co said. "Most players believe there is little likelihood the Fed will raise rates here."
U.S. blue chip stocks and bonds rose yesterday as weaker-than-forecast manufacturing data heightened expectations the Federal Reserve would leave rates alone.
The Dow Jones Industrial Average finished up 49.54 points at 7722.33 on Tuesday.
This morning, the Standard & Poor's 500 futures rose 1.75 points to 903. The long bond rose 7/32 to yield 6.73 percent.

"The only surprise here would be if the Fed raised rates," Peter Cardillo, director of research at Westfalia Investments said. He said stock market valuations already assumed the Federal Reserve would not raise rates.
Stocks and bonds were also awaiting a key employment report for June, due out on Thursday, for any sign of wage inflation, analysts said.
The only data expected before the Federal Reserve announcement were factory orders for May, which were forecast to decline by 0.2 percent versus a previous 1.2 percent gain.
While financial markets were calm about the interest rate outlook, investors would soon start turning their focus to the coming corporate earnings reporting period, analysts said.

"There continues to be a tug-of-war between those who think the Federal Reserve will not raise rates and those who think corporate earnings will be the more important factor over the coming weeks," Ackerman said.

Among companies which have already reported results, Nike Corp posted fourth quarter earnings of $0.52 per share versus $0.45 per share in the year-ago fourth quarter and a First Call consensus earnings estimate of $0.53 per share.
"My guess is that in the third quarter, the focus will be on individual stocks rather than the market as a whole," Cardillo said. He said he expected Nike to slump today.
Japan's Nikkei average closed up 20.90 points at 20,196.42.
In London, the FTSE 100 was off 6.2 points at 4722.1. U.S. stocks were mixed in quiet trade in London.
The dollar trimmed earlier losses against the yen in Tokyo, trading at 114.45/55 yen. In Europe, the dollar was firm against the mark, trading at 1.7505/15 marks.

The Wall Street Journal said in its Heard on the Street column that arbitragers suffered large losses on their holdings of Office Depot Inc, after a federal court ruling barring its proposed merger with Staples Inc.

The New York Times said in its Market Place column that many analysts believe front-office applications are the biggest growth area in the software industry and investors can still participate in the growth if they pick stocks carefully.
